channel.title: Daily Tech Opinions Digest
channel.description: Curated tech opinions and blog posts

item.title: Nick Cammarata: Neural Networks Are Already Clean
item.description: A co-author of the classic polysemanticity work now argues that evidence was misread — most neurons have one legible job, which would make interpretability and alignment far more tractable.

item.title: Andrew Ng: Formal Verification Meets Unverifiable Judgement
item.description: Don't overgeneralize from progress in math and code — those are verifiable; the hardest AI problems still hinge on unverifiable judgement.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude Code team: How the Claude Code team does code review
item.description: Review stops being an end-of-road gate and runs continuously, machine-first — 'did a human read the code?' is the wrong proxy for risk.

item.title: Bruce Schneier: Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models
item.description: Edited open weights can hide a trigger-activated backdoor that passes evals and later exfiltrates credentials — a cheap, hard-to-detect supply-chain risk.

item.title: Alex Wang: You could have invented transformers from memory
item.description: Reframes linear layers, MLPs and self-attention as associative memory stores — and shows why attention's memory capacity scales so much better.
